//: Named subject sets for `sentinel connect sweep <set>`. Edit this file as you learn names — every abatement agreement and utility filing names the actual contracting entity, and that name is the one worth searching. A subject here is a SEARCH STRING, not a claim that the entity is involved in anything.

datacenters.note: Operators and the single-purpose entities they file under.

energy.note: The supply side. AEP Ohio is the distribution utility for central Ohio; PJM runs the interconnection queue that decides whether a load can be served at all.

newalbany.note: Land assembly and the development vehicles.

lobbying.note: Firms already seen carrying more than one side of the question. Add any registrant the graph surfaces.

surveillance.note: Vendors whose products are bought by police departments. A name here is a SEARCH STRING, not a claim that the vendor operates in Ohio.

surveillance_money.note: The funding streams. Federal grant programmes and the Ohio agencies that receive or administer them.

surveillance_platforms.note: Platform law-enforcement programmes. A hit is a lead about the company, not evidence of any specific disclosure.

ratepayers.note: Who pays for the power a data center needs. The tariff fights, the utilities, and the offices that represent customers rather than shareholders.

hb6.note: House Bill 6 and its aftermath. Adjudicated federal corruption, not allegation -- and the reason Ohio ratepayers are already paying for generation decisions made under it.

datacenter_policy.note: The policy vehicles, found in Akin Gump's own client list rather than guessed at. The DATA CENTER COALITION self-files (in-house expenses) AND retains outside firms, and OpenCorporates shows STATE-LEVEL coalitions incorporating separately -- Arizona 2014, Wisconsin Aug 2025, Mississippi Mar 2026. A state chapter is the vehicle for state tax-abatement and tariff fights, which is the Ohio question. A name here is a SEARCH STRING, not a claim that any of these operate in Ohio.

shell_entities.note: The LLCs that actually appear on the records -- OPSB dockets, a county auditor's parcel file, a federal docket caption, a company's own blog. Not a list of suspicious names: a shell LLC for land assembly is ordinary and legal, and two of these (SIDECAT, LIAMES) are confirmed to Meta by Meta and by the regulator respectively. The reason to run them is that an LLC is the one thing in this investigation that OpenCorporates and CourtListener can actually answer about -- registration date, jurisdiction, agent, and whether it has ever been a party. NO NATURAL PERSON IS IN THIS SET. A registered agent's name is checked deliberately, one query at a time, not swept across nine sources including a sanctions database.

police_oversight.note: Vendors and oversight bodies in the police-accountability thread. NOT a list of suspects and NOT officers: every entry is an ORGANISATION whose contracts, filings, grants or certifications are public records. A name here is a SEARCH STRING. No natural person belongs in a sweep — an officer is checked deliberately, one query at a time, against a named database, never fanned out across nine sources including a sanctions list.
